transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you for fitting me in, I, uh, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

Well, I suppose... I don't want to make a fuss or sound ungrateful for my life, but... it's just that I keep thinking my wife and the kids would be better off if I just didn't wake up. It's awful to say, I know. I'm sorry to even bring it up. And I guess lately I've been saying things out loud like... well, that I don't really need to see another winter. 

Is that... is that the sort of thing you wanted to know? I want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
Have you ever felt this way before, like you didn’t want to wake up or didn’t want to see another winter?

No, I... I don't believe I have. I've always tried to be a steady sort of man, you know? Kept my chin up, provided for the family. I've never really had these kinds of... well, ungrateful thoughts before. 

It just seems to have crept up on me lately, for some reason. I hope that's an alright answer? I just wouldn't want you to think I've been complaining my whole life, because I really haven't. I've always tried to be very thankful for what I have.
When did these feelings of not wanting to wake up and thinking your family would be better off without you first start?

Well, um... let me think. I suppose it's been... oh, about a year and a month ago. Yes, right around then. That's, um, that's when my old bowling partner passed away. 

I know it probably sounds a bit foolish to let something like that upset me so much, especially at my age. We all have to go sometime, I know that, and I shouldn't be making a fuss. But... well, I guess since he died, these thoughts just sort of started coming around and getting stuck in my head. I really hope I'm not overreacting or making too much out of it. 

Is that the kind of timeline you were looking for, Doctor? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right details.
Have you ever experienced a period before this one where you felt persistently down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

No, I... I really don't think so. I mean, everyone gets a little blue sometimes, right? Just a bad day here or there, which is perfectly normal. But nothing like this... nothing where it just stuck around and made me feel so, well, useless. 

Before all this started last year, I always enjoyed my days. I liked keeping busy, taking care of the house, spending time with my wife. I've had a very blessed life, you see, so I'd have no real reason to feel hopeless before now. I'd hate for you to think I'm the sort of person who just wallows in things. 

I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, Doctor. Does that answer your question alright?
Have you ever had a period in your life before this one where you felt down or hopeless nearly every day for at least two weeks in a row?

No, Doctor, I... I really haven't. I'm sorry if I didn't make that clear before. I haven't ever had a stretch like that, not for two weeks, not even close to that, really. 

I've always been the sort to just, you know, brush off a bad mood and get on with it. There's always chores to do, or someone who needs a hand, so I've never let myself get bogged down like that in the past. It wouldn't be right to just sit around feeling sorry for myself when I've had so much to be grateful for. 

I really hope I'm giving you the answers you need. I'm trying my best to remember everything correctly for you. Is there... is there something else I should be thinking of?
Have you ever had a time in your life before this current period when you felt so down or hopeless that it really interfered with your daily life, even for just a short while?

No, no, I... I really don't think so. I'm sorry, I know you keep asking, and I feel like I'm giving you the wrong answer or... or not being helpful. But truly, before my friend passed, I was always able to keep up with everything. 

I've always prided myself on being reliable, you know? Taking care of the yard, helping my wife around the house... I wouldn't let a bad mood stop me from doing my duties. That just wouldn't be fair to her. I've always managed to just push through any little slumps. 

I'm sorry, I really hope I'm not frustrating you by saying the same thing. Am I... am I misunderstanding what you're asking, Doctor? I want to make sure I'm doing this right.

Have you ever experienced a time in your life before your friend passed away where you felt down or hopeless for a period long enough that it started to weigh on you, even if it didn’t interfere with your daily life?

No, Doctor, I... I promise I'm not trying to be difficult, I just... I really can't recall any time like that. I've always been a pretty steady person, you know? Even if I felt a little blue, I'd just focus on my blessings and it would pass right over. 

I never let anything weigh on me too much back then. I always thought it was important to keep a positive attitude, especially for my wife. I didn't want to be a burden or a complainer. 

I'm so sorry if I'm not giving you the information you're looking for. I feel terrible that you have to keep asking me this in different ways. I'm really trying to search my memory for you. Am I doing okay? I just want to be as helpful as I can.
Doctor: Since your friend passed away, have you had any days where you felt so down, hopeless, or lost interest in almost all activities for most of the day, nearly every day?

Well... yes, I suppose I have. I hate to admit it, because I know I should be doing better. But since he passed... I just haven't been myself. 

I used to be so active, you know? I always looked forward to our weekly bridge games, and... and tending to my garden. I even used to help out with the cooking at church, and I loved going to Cubs games when I could. But lately... lately I just sit in my chair most of the day. I try to get up and do things, I really do, but I just... I can't seem to make myself care about any of it anymore. It all just feels so empty. 

I feel awful even saying it out loud. It sounds so ungrateful, doesn't it? I know I should be trying harder to keep busy. I hope you don't think less of me for letting things go like this. I'm really trying my best to answer you honestly... is this the kind of thing you needed to know?
Before the time your friend passed away, have you ever had a period where you felt down or hopeless enough that you thought you might need help, even if you didn’t ask for it?

No, no, I... I never thought I needed help back then. I really didn't. I'm sorry, I know we keep going over this, and I feel like I'm just being stubborn or... or giving you a hard time. But honestly, I always managed just fine. 

I mean, everyone has a bad day here and there, right? But I never thought, "Oh, I need to go see a doctor about this." I just... I'd count my blessings, maybe spend a little extra time in the garden, and I'd be right as rain. I always believed a man should be able to handle his own moods, you know? Not bother other people with them. 

I really hope I'm not making your job difficult by not having a better answer for you. I'm trying so hard to think back, but I just never felt that way before... before all this. Am I making sense, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Have you ever had a period in your life before this one where you felt so down, hopeless, or lost interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

No, Doctor, I... I really haven't. I know you've asked me this a few different ways now, and I feel just awful that my answer is still the same. I'm really not trying to be a bother or hide anything from you, I promise. 

It's just that, well, before my friend passed... I was always so steady. Even if I felt a little down for a day or two, I'd never let it drag on for weeks. I'd just pull myself up by the bootstraps, you know? Get out in the yard, keep busy, make sure my wife was taken care of. I always thought it was my duty to keep a smile on my face. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like a broken record. I just never had a time like what I'm going through right now. Is it okay that I don't have a different answer for you? I really am trying my best to be a good patient.
Since your friend passed away, have you had a period where you felt down or lost interest in most things for most of the day, nearly every day, that lasted at least two weeks?

Yes, Doctor... yes, it's definitely been longer than two weeks. I'm so sorry, I probably should have made that clearer right from the start. I didn't mean to make you ask the same sort of thing again. 

Ever since he passed, it's just been... well, it's been every day. I keep thinking, "Tomorrow, I'll get up and tend to the yard," but the weeks just sort of bleed together, and I end up staying in my chair. I feel terrible admitting it, like I'm just an old man feeling sorry for himself when I really ought to be counting my blessings. 

I hope I'm giving you the right answers. I really am trying to be helpful... is that what you needed to know about the timeline?
Doctor: Have you had these feelings of being down or losing interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for as long as two years or more since your friend passed away?

Oh, no, Doctor, not quite that long. I'm so sorry if I confused you or made it sound worse than it is. I really didn't mean to mislead you. 

It's... well, this has been going on since my bowling partner died. That was about a year and a month ago now. I'd like to think I wouldn't let myself be this much of a bother to everyone for two whole years without figuring out how to pull myself together. 

I hope that clears things up for your notes. Am I doing alright answering these for you? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and giving you exactly what you need.
Have you had these feelings of being down or losing interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for as long as two years or more since your friend passed away?

Oh, dear, I'm so sorry, Doctor. Did I not explain that right just a moment ago? I feel just terrible making you ask me the exact same thing again. I must be getting my words all tangled up and wasting your time. 

But no, it hasn't been two years. Like I was trying to say—and I apologize if I didn't make it clear—it's just been about a year and a month. I would be so ashamed of myself if I had let this drag on for two whole years without snapping out of it. I really am trying not to be a nuisance to my wife or to you. 

I hope I didn't upset you by making you repeat the question. Does that timeline make sense for your paperwork, or did I misunderstand what you were asking me? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Oh, I... I'm so sorry, Doctor. I feel like I'm doing a terrible job of explaining things to you today. I must be making your job so difficult, and I really don't mean to. 

You see, it hasn't been just a specific two weeks... it's been the whole time. Every day since he passed, for that whole year and a month. There hasn't been a time where I felt better and then it came back for two weeks... it's just been a constant, steady thing. I really should have explained that better the first time you asked. I feel so foolish for not being clearer. 

I'm probably making a mountain out of a molehill, really. I should be able to just shake this off. But... does that answer your question better? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details so you can do your job. Am I doing okay?

I hope that's the right answer... I mean, I hope that's helpful for your evaluation. I'm just a normal, quiet old man, really. Does that sound alright to you?

Oh, dear... I think we might have just talked about this, and I feel so terrible if I confused you earlier. I really am trying my best to be helpful, I promise. 

But no, I... I've never felt this way for two whole years. It's really just been since my friend passed away a little over a year ago. Have you ever had a time in your life where you felt down or lost interest in most things for most of the day, nearly every day, for as long as two years?
